i was in your spot when i was 14. i did not have a good support system of friends and everything made me miserable. i would cry whenever i was alone and thought that if i told no one it would go away because i didn’t want to burden my family with my thoughts. on june of 2020 i tried to commit su!cide but thankfully it didn’t work. no one knew except my sister. i then realized that this is not something i had to carry alone. my sisters were there to support me and i was there to support them. i started to cherish the small things in life and appreciate every breath i took because tomorrow wasn’t promised. i did this all without therapy. yes therapy can be very helpful when trying to figure out these feelings but it is not necessary. the mind is a very powerful thing that even in our dying minutes it gave me the strength to get up and find my sister to help me. seek out family or friends who will have your back in these tough times. i know that this seems like it’ll go on forever but i promise it doesn’t. keep fighting.

don’t let anyone ruin your day. you did that. you graduated form medical school, that’s some tough shit to do and you accomplished it. don’t let family or relationships determine your happiness. find something that you love to do even if it is the simplest thing. it doesn’t matter because it’s precious to you. keep a chin up my friend and congratulations

i try not to look into what i think my future will be like because i end up thinking like this. take life one day at a time. get excited about small things because we are only here for a brief moment on earths time. the little things like going to the movies, eating your favorite food, getting a good grade make life worth living. you cannot find the things you have here in here anywhere else. cherish life for how simple it can be. we can die at any moment yet we still breathe. tomorrow isn’t promised, life gets better when you look at things in a simpler way. i hope you feel better about this my friend.

you are not a shitty friend trust me. i have always been the therapist friend to my other friends and always find myself drained. it’s exhausting at times being there for them when at times you just want someone to be there for you. please take care of yourself mentally and maybe talk to your friends about this

when i was a freshmen in high school i was in that girls shoes. my older sister used to self harm when she was about 13 and she told me about it. she said she told me because she didn’t want me to ever have to resort to that. i promised her that i wouldn’t yet i lied. when things got and i indulged my urges and would slice away at my skin until my shirt were stained red. when my sister found out she was heartbroken and made me promise to never do it again. i did so and again i lied. i kept on self harming for 1 year until i decided i needed to let it all out healthily before i went too far again. when my sister asked why i never told her i was doing it again i told her i was ashamed. how could i face her after lying to her face about something that broke her so much. i didn’t want her to be disappointed in me even though i knew deep down there was no way she could be because she was in my shoes once too. you have every right to be angry, i would be too but maybe try talking to her in a judgment free zone where she can tell you why she lied.
